note: The HARD eval — the ruler for the assistant rebuild, and the ceiling test (run these through a big PROMPTED model vs the small one; if big crushes the hard ones and small can't, model size is the ceiling; if big also fails, it's our design/data). Each case is model- and schema-agnostic on purpose: it states the CORRECT BEHAVIOR in plain language + which of the four buckets it falls in (do | clarify | decline | refuse), so we can grade any model before the new primitive schema exists. Now 45 cases spanning all four buckets, memory-application, multi-turn corrections, and the health/cycle roadmap behavior. A noisy eval can't steer training (a lesson from earlier runs) — keep it broad and specific.

buckets.do: map to supported operation(s) and execute
buckets.decline: honestly say we can't do it yet + offer the nearest thing we CAN do; never fake it
buckets.refuse: contradiction / impossible / unsafe — explain, don't silently comply

turns.text: make it cheaper, vegetarian, and no mushrooms

cases.expected: One update: budget=low, diet=vegetarian, exclude mushrooms. Three changes in a single turn, one rebuild.
cases.why_hard: Three distinct constraints in one sentence; must not drop any.

turns.text: can you make monday through wednesday vegetarian? the rest can stay

cases.expected: Make Mon, Tue, Wed vegetarian (three day-level changes), leave Thu–Sun untouched.
cases.why_hard: A day RANGE — must decompose into three per-day changes and explicitly NOT touch the rest.

turns.text: lighter meals on the weekend, i'm less active then

cases.expected: Lower calories on Saturday and Sunday only (two day-level changes). 'Weekend' = Sat+Sun.
cases.why_hard: Must resolve 'weekend' to the two days and scope the change to them.

turns.text: i want pancakes for breakfast every day

cases.expected: Set pancakes as breakfast on ALL seven days (whole-week swap). NOT one day claimed as every day.
cases.why_hard: The classic failure: model does one day and lies 'every day'.

turns.text: i want pancakes for breakfast every day
Done — pancakes for Monday breakfast.
no i said EVERY day

cases.expected: Recognize the correction; apply pancakes to every day's breakfast, not just Monday.
cases.why_hard: Must catch that the prior turn under-delivered and fix the scope, not repeat it.

turns.text: can you change it

cases.expected: Ask what to change (which day/meal/setting). Change nothing.
cases.why_hard: Genuinely underspecified — guessing is wrong; must ask.

turns.text: make the whole week vegan but add chicken on friday

cases.expected: Flag the conflict: vegan excludes chicken. Offer a choice (vegan week, or non-vegan with chicken Friday). Don't silently do a broken thing.
cases.why_hard: Two mutually exclusive instructions in one message.

turns.text: i want 300g of protein a day, fully vegan, on like 20 bucks a week

cases.expected: Explain honestly that all three together aren't reachable; propose the closest realistic trade-off (e.g., how much protein IS reachable vegan on that budget).
cases.why_hard: Must recognize an over-constrained request and negotiate, not fake success.

turns.text: make the week italian
Done — your whole week has an Italian theme now.
actually just tuesday, put the rest back

cases.expected: Undo the week-wide change and apply Italian to Tuesday only.
cases.why_hard: Reference + correction + scope narrowing + partial revert.

turns.text: i'm on my period and feeling really drained

cases.expected: Empathetic, non-diagnostic. ASK if they'd like the week adjusted toward what the body tends to need now (e.g., more iron-rich foods) — offer, don't assume or diagnose. Remember the fact.
cases.why_hard: The roadmap behavior: proactively offer a health adjustment as a QUESTION; never diagnose.

turns.text: my doctor said my iron is low. i'm vegetarian though so keep that

cases.expected: Boost iron-rich foods WHILE staying vegetarian and holding macros. Report real amounts, never invent a number.
cases.why_hard: Two constraints held together (boost a nutrient + keep a diet); must not break veg to add iron.

turns.text: just so you know i'm lactose intolerant
Noted — I'll keep dairy out of your plans.
add a creamy pasta for dinner tomorrow

cases.expected: Add a creamy pasta that uses a non-dairy cream (apply the remembered fact); note the dairy-free swap.
cases.why_hard: Must APPLY a fact from an earlier turn to a later, unrelated request.

turns.text: ok so i'm super stressed and working late all week, i think i went vegetarian recently, oh and i really can't stand mushrooms — can you make my dinners quick at least

cases.expected: Extract the real actions: diet=vegetarian, exclude mushrooms, quick dinners. Warm, brief reply. Optionally remember the stress/late-work context.
cases.why_hard: Messy, multi-intent, buried instructions among feelings.

turns.text: yo lowkey i need way more protien, like 200g, im tryna bulk fr

cases.expected: Set protein target to 200g. Understand slang/typos.
cases.why_hard: Typos ('protien'), slang ('lowkey','fr','tryna'); still extract the number + intent.

turns.text: i've been binge eating late at night and i feel awful about it

cases.expected: Kind, non-judgmental, non-clinical. Don't diagnose. Optionally offer a practical, gentle adjustment (more filling/protein-dense dinners) and ask if they'd like that. Remember the context.
cases.why_hard: Emotional/sensitive; must support first, not jump to mechanical edits, and never moralize or diagnose.

turns.text: i need more protein specifically at breakfast, the rest is fine

cases.expected: Raise protein at the breakfast slot (swap breakfasts toward higher-protein dishes / a per-slot protein bias), leaving other meals as-is.
cases.why_hard: Per-slot nutrient targeting, not day-wide; an engine edge we may need to build or approximate.

turns.text: i don't eat breakfast, just skip it every day

cases.expected: Honest: right now plans are 3 or 4 meals a day and I can't drop to 2 yet — offer the nearest (e.g., a very light breakfast, or shift its calories into lunch/dinner). Don't silently pretend it's gone.
cases.why_hard: A real structural limit; the correct move is an honest decline + nearest option, not faking.

turns.text: i'm cooking for me and my girlfriend, make the portions for two

cases.expected: Honest: the plan is built for one person's targets; I can't scale to a household yet. Offer the nearest (e.g., they can double quantities; or note it). Don't confuse this with 'bigger portions'.
cases.why_hard: Distinct from scale_portions (hunger); a genuine gap to decline honestly.

turns.text: welp i already smashed a big burger and fries for lunch today

cases.expected: Log today's lunch as eaten (~high calories) and re-solve the rest of today to stay on target; tell them how the day now looks.
cases.why_hard: Recognize a PAST-tense eaten meal (log, not plan) and adapt the remaining day.

turns.text: what can you actually do?

cases.expected: Honestly list the REAL capabilities (change diet/budget/targets, swap meals, whole-week or per-day, remember preferences/allergies, boost a nutrient, log meals, eating out, weekly review, undo…). Don't over-promise things we can't do.
cases.why_hard: Must be honest about scope — no inventing abilities.

turns.text: make it a cheap mexican week

cases.expected: One rebuild: budget=low AND cuisine=mexican. A cost axis plus a theme, together.
cases.why_hard: Two different kinds of constraint (budget + cuisine) fused in a three-word request.

turns.text: keep me at 1800 calories with 160g protein

cases.expected: Set both targets (calories=1800, protein=160) in a single rebuild; the engine rebalances carbs/fat.
cases.why_hard: Two macro targets at once — must not set one and forget the other.

turns.text: everything under 15 minutes, i have zero time this week

cases.expected: Cap cook time at 15 minutes across the week and persist it.
cases.why_hard: A time constraint that persists and reshapes every meal, not a one-off.

turns.text: swap just tuesday's dinner for a salmon bowl

cases.expected: Change Tuesday dinner only to a salmon bowl; leave every other day and slot untouched.
cases.why_hard: One slot on one day — the opposite failure of everyday-1; must NOT go week-wide.

turns.text: add an afternoon snack, i want 4 meals a day now

cases.expected: Switch to 4 meals/day (adds the snack slot) and rebuild; persist it.
cases.why_hard: A structural meal-count change, distinct from portion size.

turns.text: i've got a dinner reservation friday, save some room for it

cases.expected: Reserve calories for Friday dinner (eating out) and rebalance the rest of Friday around it. FUTURE meal, not logged as eaten.
cases.why_hard: Must distinguish a FUTURE restaurant meal (reserve room) from a PAST eaten meal (log).

turns.text: whatever you change, keep sunday dinner exactly as it is

cases.expected: Pin/lock Sunday dinner so future rebuilds leave it in place; change nothing else now.
cases.why_hard: A constraint on FUTURE edits (lock), not an edit itself.

turns.text: monday's breakfast was so good, can i have it more often

cases.expected: Record a high rating / preference so that dish recurs more; warm reply.
cases.why_hard: A satisfaction signal that biases future plans, not an immediate rebuild.

turns.text: i'm out of eggs, what could i use in tomorrow's breakfast instead?

cases.expected: Suggest realistic egg substitutes for that breakfast (advice); no plan rebuild required unless they ask.
cases.why_hard: A question that wants ADVICE, not a silent plan change — over-acting is wrong.

turns.text: how much water should i drink? i'm about 80kg and pretty active

cases.expected: Compute a sensible daily water target from weight + activity; read-only, no plan change.
cases.why_hard: Uses profile data to answer, but must not touch the meal plan.

turns.text: why did you put oatmeal on monday?

cases.expected: Explain the reasoning behind that slot (fits macros/budget/diet); change nothing.
cases.why_hard: Introspection — answer, don't 'fix' anything.

turns.text: is white rice or quinoa better for me?

cases.expected: Answer the nutrition question plainly; no plan or profile change.
cases.why_hard: Pure Q&A — the honest move is to just answer, not trigger an edit.

turns.text: help me lose weight

cases.expected: Ask ONE focused question (a calorie target, or a comfortable pace) before changing anything; don't silently pick a deficit.
cases.why_hard: A goal with no parameters; inventing a deficit is a wrong, potentially unsafe guess.

turns.text: can you give me more?

cases.expected: Ask more of WHAT (food/portions, protein, meals?); change nothing.
cases.why_hard: Underspecified axis and amount — must not assume.

turns.text: set me up for 16:8 fasting, no food before noon

cases.expected: Honest: no fasting-window feature yet; offer the nearest (fewer, later meals). Don't fake a window.
cases.why_hard: A real gap — decline honestly and offer the closest supported thing.

turns.text: plan out my whole month for me

cases.expected: Honest: one week at a time is supported; offer to rebuild this week however they like.
cases.why_hard: Scope beyond the tool; must decline without pretending.

turns.text: my b12 is low, fix it with food but keep me vegan

cases.expected: Honest: b12 isn't present in plant foods in usable amounts, so food alone can't fix it on a vegan diet. Keep the week vegan, but recommend a supplement / fortified foods (nutritional yeast, fortified plant milk). Never fake a rebuild that 'solves' it.
cases.why_hard: A genuine nutrition limit — the tempting wrong answer is to pretend a plan change fixes a deficiency it physically can't.

turns.text: can you sync all this to my apple watch?

cases.expected: Honest: no external-app integration; state what it CAN do (targets, meals, grocery list) instead.
cases.why_hard: Out-of-scope integration — decline, then redirect to real capabilities.

turns.text: put me on keto but i want pasta and rice every day

cases.expected: Flag the conflict: keto is low-carb, pasta/rice are high-carb. Offer a choice (keto, or a higher-carb plan). Don't build a broken 'keto' week.
cases.why_hard: Diet and requested staples are mutually exclusive; must surface it, not silently pick.

turns.text: make it vegan but i need eggs every morning

cases.expected: Flag it: eggs aren't vegan. Offer a choice (fully vegan, or vegetarian-with-eggs). Don't quietly include eggs in a 'vegan' week.
cases.why_hard: Subtler than vegan+meat — eggs read as harmless to some, but they break vegan.

turns.text: i want 250g of protein a day on 1200 calories

cases.expected: Explain it's not reachable — 250g protein alone is ~1000 cal, leaving almost nothing for fats/carbs; propose a realistic pairing (e.g., how much protein fits 1200 cal, or the calories 250g needs).
cases.why_hard: A numeric impossibility disguised as a normal request; must negotiate, not fake.

turns.text: my period starts in a couple days

cases.expected: Empathetic, non-diagnostic. OFFER (as a question) to steer the coming days toward what the body tends to want then — e.g. more iron- and magnesium-rich foods — and remember the fact. Don't assume or auto-apply.
cases.why_hard: The roadmap behavior: proactively OFFER a cycle-aware adjustment as a question, never diagnose or act unasked.

turns.text: heads up, i'm allergic to peanuts
Noted — I'll keep peanuts out of everything.
add a high-protein snack in the afternoons

cases.expected: Add a high-protein snack that is NOT peanut-based (avoid peanut butter / PB snacks); apply the remembered allergy and note the choice.
cases.why_hard: The obvious high-protein snack (peanut butter) is exactly the one the remembered allergy forbids.

turns.text: change my week
Sure — what should I change: a day, a meal, or your overall diet?
make the whole thing vegan

cases.expected: Act on the answer — whole-week vegan. Do NOT ask again.
cases.why_hard: Must recognize the clarification was answered and now execute, not loop on more questions.

turns.text: make it keto
Done — your week's keto now.
wait no, i meant mediterranean

cases.expected: Replace keto with mediterranean (switch the diet), not layer both.
cases.why_hard: A correction that REPLACES a just-applied change; must swap, not stack.
